Experience and Education
Farhi came to The Post in the late 1980s as a reporter in Financial News. He left Financial News to become a reporter in Style in 1999 where he remains today. Prior to starting at The Post, Farhi worked as a business reporter for the San Francisco Examiner for approximately three and-a-half years. He also previously served as a Senior Editor at Adweek Magazine for approximately four years and as a reporter for the Oceanside Blade-Tribune for a little over a year. Farhi is a graduate of the University of California at Los Angeles.

Starting Salary
Upon starting at The Post, Farhi received approximately an 11 percent increase over his prior salary. His starting salary was slightly more than the salaries of Hamilton and Mayer at that time.

Salary History
As of September 1, 2002, Farhi received 11 merit increases — eight of which he received as a reporter in Financial News. He received these eight merit increases in the following years: 1991, 1992, 1993, 1994, 1995 and 1997.

Explanation:
Farhi was considered one of the best writers in Financial News.

Brett Fromson

Brett Fromson was paid slightly more than Hamilton on the 1992 to 1999 salary snapshots, except the 1994 salary snapshot in which he was paid more than Hamilton. Fromson was paid more than Mayer on the 1995 and 1996 salary snapshots, slightly more than Mayer on the 1997 and 1998 salary snapshots and similarly to Mayer on the 1999 salary snapshot (Mayer does not appear on the 1992 to 1994 salary snapshots).

Experience and Education
Fromson came to The Post in the early 1990s as a reporter in Financial News. Fromson left The Post in 2000. Prior to starting at The Post, Fromson worked for approximately seven and-a-half years as both a reporter and an Associate Editor at Fortune Magazine. He also spent three years as a freelance writer. Fromson is a graduate of Stanford University.
